target_customer: Patients and employers (pop-up clinics), later digital first primary care patients
problem: Primary care is hard to access and uses outdated software.
business_model: Insurance billed primary care plus employer clinics

founders.name: George Favvas
founders.background_notes: Third party profile; names JS Boulanger as co-founder, roles unverified

technical_complexity.rationale: Built patient apps, scheduling, billing and records software alongside clinical operations.

defensibility.rationale: Clinic operations and payer contracts are hard to scale but telemedicine is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors Pager, Heal and HealthTap noted in 2018; later One Medical was bought by Amazon.

market_need_then: Employers wanted onsite primary care; company reported 20,000 patients and 2.6M annualized revenue by Nov 2018.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name; positioning lives in the product.

pivots.why: Per company timeline, coincides with COVID

outcome_analysis: Circle Medical raised 3.5 million dollars in 2018 with about 2.6 million dollars annualized revenue and a claim of near profitability, then shifted to digital first care in March 2020. WELL Health Technologies, an early investor, made a corporate majority investment reported at 14.3 million dollars in November 2020 per CB Insights; the company remains active.
notes: Founder identities from aggregator profiles. 2020 WELL Health deal figure of 14.3M from one aggregator, unverified, not recorded as a round. Aggregators show conflicting totals (7.04M to 12.5M). A MobiHealthNews headline mentions a 29M raise that was not read, so unverified. Competitors dated at batch not found. Exit left none because a majority stake is not confirmed as an acquisition.
